findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: map_err to a typed I/O or ParseError and propagate via Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input or malformed lines
findings.failure_mode: corrupt or user-supplied data crashes the application instead of yielding a typed parse error
findings.fix: parse with map_err to a typed Invalid or Parse error; use split_once with get/split for bounded access

findings.problem: lossy width cast: .unwrap() as u16 — u32 values outside 0..=65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range values wrap silently, producing invalid domain data (e.g. 70000 becomes 4464)
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexing on a Vec produced by split, no length guard
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Invalid) then access fields by index on the 2-element array

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O side effect inside data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: purity of the core is broken; side effects leak into the data layer making it untestable and non-deterministic
findings.fix: move all logging/printing to the imperative shell; the core parser should be a pure function returning Records

findings.problem: load_packets couples file I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be unit-tested for parsing correctness without mocking the filesystem; violates core/shell split
findings.fix: split into a pure parse_records(&[RecordInput]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> core function and a shell function that reads the file and delegates

findings.problem: collects every split part into Vec<String> with to_string() allocations before extracting two fields
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per line; for large files this causes excessive GC pressure and memory churn
findings.fix: use split_once(',') then trim each part; borrow &str where possible; avoid intermediate Vec<String>

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve — unbounded growth with no allocation-failure handling
findings.failure_mode: if the file has many lines the Vec may fail to reallocate; no typed Allocation error is returned
findings.fix: estimate line count, call values.try_reserve(estimated).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation)?, then collect

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 — no newtypes, no domain invariants, no validation at construction
findings.failure_mode: any code can create invalid Records (empty name, out-of-range value) because the struct has no invariants
findings.fix: use newtype for name (e.g. RecordName(String)) with a smart constructor; add Record::try_new(name, value) that validates invariants

findings.problem: No typed error enum exists — all failures silently panic via unwrap() or indexing
findings.failure_mode: consumer cannot distinguish I/O errors, parse errors, overflow, or malformed-line errors
findings.fix: define a typed error enum (e.g. enum PacketError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Overflow, Empty }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError>

findings.problem: Record owns String for name — always allocates even for short-lived or borrowed data
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation overhead; caller cannot pass borrowed data through the type
findings.fix: use Cow<'a, str> for name or accept a lifetime-parameterized Record<'a> with &'a str

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_packets throughput or allocation profiling
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, cargo-flamegraph) for the parsing hot path
no allocation tracing (e.g. dhat-rs, alloc counters) for Vec growth behavior
no second-ring test or fuzzing evidence for malformed input handling (would be relevant once typed errors exist)
no CLI/command invocation evidence — no binary target defined in Cargo.toml
residual_risk: The crate is a single-file parser with multiple panics on untrusted input (I/O, parse, index, cast). The functional core is not isolated from the imperative shell. Until a typed error taxonomy, split_once-based parsing, checked conversions, and core/shell separation are in place, the failure surface is broad and all failures manifest as panics rather than recoverable errors. Static review only; no commands were run.
